method: Manual body review, no production/test modifications. Coverage is not execution; join only completed per-node manifests. Older coverage entries reread against current source.

requirements.rationale: Restart production lifespan with stable boot specs; repeated boot reuses session/request, identity preserved. Failed connector isolated, remaining endpoint ready; uncertain failed start stays quarantined on restart.
requirements.limitations: Disposable production bootstrap and synthetic peers; native processes qualified separately.

requirements.rationale: Concurrent closes overlap final native event and EOF; same durable close operation, one connector close, one captured final, closing entry released. Projection failure/repeated close recovery is separately exercised.
requirements.limitations: Controlled peer EOF, no native model. Error and EOF use the shared cleanup path.

requirements.rationale: Production factories reuse exact native connection for two endpoints, one detach preserves process and sibling durable result, last close observes stop. Active-close terminal correlation and stale-terminal uncertainty tested.
requirements.limitations: Owned Codex protocol peer. Real Codex multiplex also passed separately at752cd72, not counted in this full-suite manifest.

requirements.rationale: Malformed/unsupported Pi readiness fails with protocol_incompatible diagnostic and quarantines binding while Codex can still open; invalid Codex native thread identity never becomes ready or receives turn/start.
requirements.limitations: Synthetic incompatible protocol peers; native binary version qualification is separately controlled.

requirements.rationale: Operator recovery requires current attempt/epoch/state, reason and duplicate-risk acknowledgement. REST/MCP/stdio decisions agree. One audit decision releases the same logical inbox without rewriting unknown transport facts; pending native calls/live runtimes prevent takeover. A late terminal stays historical and cannot consume or publish after release.
requirements.limitations: Synthetic peers and disposable stores. Explicit takeover acknowledges possible duplicate external work; no exactly-once or native replay claim.

requirements.rationale: Urgent interrupt proceeds while normal write is blocked and binds expected operation. Stale native turn is rejected, queued steer is rejected after its turn ends, and later delivery/administrative turns cannot overtake a retry-wait lane.
requirements.limitations: Controlled event barriers and synthetic peers; does not claim preemption of arbitrary OS-blocked native code.

requirements.rationale: After restoring the persisted RUNNING/active crash state and replacing the owner through production bootstrap, historical runtime becomes unknown and quarantined; its presence closes while an independent canonical session remains active. Native end is not fabricated and no runtime is relaunched.
requirements.limitations: Deterministic persisted crash cut, not OS process killing; exact owner death is qualified by separate crash campaigns.

requirements.rationale: Concurrent open and operator reconciliation plus serial command deduplication are asserted.
requirements.limitations: Still need concurrent send admission to tie one operation, grant charge and native effect together.

requirements.rationale: Changed open metadata and command content conflict; one grant charge/command remains.
requirements.limitations: Changed target/context and unchanged original operation payload need explicit assertions.

requirements.rationale: Safe pre-write lane-busy attempts have bounded retries then explicit inbox release.
requirements.limitations: Lane-busy is not socket failure; test does not assert unchanged inbox lease/attempt counter across transport retries.
